quote:
**It touches no run's files, no
evidence certificate, no dossier and no entry in the tamper-evident record.**
why: "no dossier" is false as of commit f83d6e90 (PR #308, merged AFTER the #306 library work this section describes). `engine/crucible/framework/v2/console/actions.py:1898-1908` — the console's `build_dossier(run_id)` now does `_label = _labels.run_label(run_id)` and appends `["--label", _label]`. That flag lands in `engine/crucible/framework/v2/report/dossier.py:751`, `_render_readme` → `L = [f"# VIGIL engagement dossier — {label or engagement_slug}", ""]`, i.e. the human name is the FIRST LINE of README.md (and reaches 00-START-HERE.html; #308's own commit message says so). And the dossier's tamper-evidence covers it: dossier.py:898 states in its own docstring "The dossier's own MANIFEST does cover the rendered documents, as it must — it is a hash of this archive's contents — and it is re-signed on every build." So renaming a run changes the downloaded dossier's bytes, changes MANIFEST.json's hashes, and produces a fresh m-of-n governance signature over it. What genuinely survives a rename is the proof bundle and the certificates — which is the property worth claiming, and the one #306's tests actually pin (identical `cert_digest` chains). I verified the call site, the render site and the manifest docstring by reading them, and confirmed #308 is in history via `git show f83d6e90`.
fix: **It touches no run's files, no evidence certificate, no part of the proof bundle and no entry in the tamper-evident record — so every certificate a customer already holds still verifies, byte for byte.** The one thing a rename does reach is deliberate: a dossier downloaded *after* a run is renamed is titled by the human name, so its readable documents differ from an earlier build and its own archive manifest is re-signed. The proof inside it is identical either way.

quote: | **Build the same run's dossier twice, under two different names** | The proof re-verifies both times with the same verdict and the same certificate identity; the two archives are **byte-for-byte identical**; and neither name appears anywhere inside either archive. |
why: The test does not build the dossier under two names. `engine/crucible/framework/v2/console/tests/test_engagement_library.py:265-267` — `_evidence_and_dossier` calls `D.build_dossier(run_dir=str(proof_run), out_zip=str(zpath), engagement_slug="acme")` with **no `label=` argument**. It sets `labels.set_run_label(...)` first, but the builder never reads the store — only `console/actions.py` does, and the test bypasses it. The same is true of `test_renaming_never_breaks_the_PROOF_BUNDLE_verification` (:337-338). So the "byte-for-byte identical" and "neither name appears anywhere inside" assertions are green because the name was never handed to the builder, not because the design confines it. The mutation control at :369 only proves the check bites on a changed `engagement_slug`, not on a changed label. This matters because it is offered to a national agency as the evidence for the section's load-bearing property, and the property it demonstrates is not the one the console's Dossier button exercises.
fix: | **Build the same run's dossier twice while the stored name changes** | The proof re-verifies both times with the same verdict and the same certificate identity, and the proof bundle inside the archive is byte-for-byte identical with identical certificate-chain digests. (The test drives the dossier builder directly, without the human name; the console's download button does pass the name through into the readable documents, so two downloads under two names are not themselves byte-identical.) |

quote:
Both make every entry cite the exact
record entry that produced it — by position and by fingerprint — so any answer can be
walked back to tamper-evident memory.
why: Not every entry. `apps/sigil/sigil/graph/schema.py:17-21` defines `CREATE NODE TABLE Project(name STRING, sessions INT64, commits INT64, documents INT64, messages INT64, PRIMARY KEY(name))` — no `anchor_seq`, no `anchor_hash`. Only Session (:22-25), Document (:27-29) and Commit (:31-33) carry the pair. Chapter 14 already states this exactly and warns against the sentence chapter 10 just wrote: 14-the-sovereign-side.md:383-388 — "**One honest exception.** The project itself carries no record number… The system's internal note that each structural node stores an anchor is a shade broader than the code delivers, and this document follows the code." Chapter 10's new text followed the internal note (schema.py:15 "Each structural node stores an anchor into the spine for provenance") instead of the table definitions, so the briefing now says two different things in two chapters about the same four tables.
fix: Both make every entry cite the exact record entry that produced it — by position and by fingerprint — so any answer can be walked back to tamper-evident memory. On the owner's side there is one honest exception, set out in chapter 14: the project node is a tally over its members rather than something any single record minted, so it carries no anchor of its own and is resolvable through the sessions, documents and commits inside it.

quote:
**They never meet.** The two halves of the system do not share a process, and the
sovereign side enforces that at the moment its own code loads: it checks that no
offensive module has been loaded alongside it and refuses to run if one has
why: The guard is per-sub-package, not "the sovereign side", and the very package this section is about is one of the ones without it. `assert_no_offense()` (apps/sigil/sigil/reuse/__init__.py:49-55) is invoked at import in agents, mesh, platform, perception, voice, scrape, ui, gesture, governor, bridge and mcp/server — but NOT in `sigil/__init__.py`, and NOT in `sigil/graph/__init__.py`, `sigil/spine/`, `sigil/vectors/`, `sigil/ingest/`, `sigil/knowledge/`, `sigil/inbound/`. I proved it by execution: with a stub `framework` module in `sys.modules`, `import sigil.graph.schema` succeeds silently, while the control `import sigil.agents` raises "SIGIL sovereignty violation: offense modules loaded: ['framework']". Footnote 6 points a checker at `apps/sigil/sigil/graph/` and at `assert_no_offense`, so a sceptical reader who follows the footnote finds the fifth picture's own package unguarded. Second qualifier: the check is a point-in-time scan of `sys.modules` performed at import (reuse/__init__.py:52-54); offensive code imported after that moment is not caught.
fix: **They never meet.** The two halves of the system do not share a process. The sovereign side enforces that with a load-time guard — it scans what is already loaded and refuses to run if any offensive module is there, raising what it calls a "sovereignty violation". Two honest limits: the guard is placed on individual sub-systems rather than on the package as a whole, and the memory graph's own sub-system is one of those it is not yet placed on; and it is a check made at the moment of loading, so it catches offensive code already present rather than code loaded afterwards. The separation that does the real work is the process and environment boundary, of which this guard is a tripwire.

quote:
- **Renaming is powerless.** A human name — "Acme, Q3 external review" — is stored in one
  small file beside the machine identity, and nothing on that path writes into a run's
  folder, an evidence certificate, a re-checkable document or the signed record.
why: Same root cause as the chapter 9 finding. The *write* path is indeed confined to one file (`console/labels.py:_save`, 0600 + atomic replace). But the *read* path is not: `console/actions.py:1898-1908` looks the run's label up on every Dossier download and passes `--label` to the builder, which puts it in README.md (`report/dossier.py:751`) and in 00-START-HERE.html. The dossier is a re-checkable document — its MANIFEST.json hashes those rendered files and is re-signed each build (`report/dossier.py:898`). So a rename is not powerless over what the next download contains; it is powerless over the certificates and the proof bundle. Verified by reading both call sites and `git show f83d6e90`.
fix: - **Renaming cannot invalidate a proof.** A human name — "Acme, Q3 external review" — is stored in one small file beside the machine identity, and nothing on that path writes into a run's folder, an evidence certificate, the proof bundle or the signed record. It does have one deliberate effect: a case file downloaded after a rename is titled by the human name, so the person opening it months later recognises the job. The proof inside it is unchanged, and the screen states the property on the page: renaming "touches no signed byte, so every certificate still verifies".

why: That file does not exist. `ls integration/vigil_integration/graph/` returns exactly `__init__.py`, `model.py`, `projector.py`, `query.py` — no `store.py`. The per-job partition store is `engine/crucible/framework/v2/graph/store.py` (its docstring: "an embedded, file-backed GRAPH STORE that is a one-way projection of the spine… A `partition` key (default "default") scopes a projection — one partition per session"), which is also the only `*graph*/store.py` in the tree. Honest note: this footnote predates the §14 rewrite (it is present at HEAD), but §14 was renamed and re-argued around it and it is the anchor the new section hands a checker, so it now mislabels a section that leans harder on being checkable.

quote:
Everything the agent does that reaches beyond its own reasoning — every
command-line tool it runs, the browser it drives, everything — passes through one thing: a
shell that can run any command at all.
why: "everything" is wrong, and the paragraph eight lines later admits it ("that gate covers **arbitrary command execution**, which is not the same as covering everything"), so the subsection contradicts itself before the correction arrives. The gate's own source states the boundary: `integration/vigil_integration/warden_gate.py:322-332` gates exactly `{"exec_command", "write_stdin"}` and classifies literally everything else A0 → auto-run, listing them as "thinking / notes / todo / web_search / apply_patch / reporting / view_image / load_skill / finish". The later enumeration of exceptions names only two (web search, proxy replay) and omits `apply_patch` — a file-writing tool attached unconditionally to every agent via the Filesystem capability (`vendor/strix/strix/agents/factory.py:460-465`, `_CUSTOM_TOOL_INPUT_FIELD_BY_NAME = {"apply_patch": "patch"}` at :67-69). It writes without passing the shell and without an owner signature. The write lands in the sandbox's own copy of the tree rather than the operator's, which is the mitigation worth stating — but the briefing states neither the tool nor the mitigation.
fix: Everything the agent does that runs a program — every command-line tool, the browser it drives — passes through one thing: a shell that can run any command at all. That shell is the gated surface; a handful of the agent's own built-in tools sit outside it and are described below.

quote: | **Documentation drift** | Two internal reference documents are stale on the screen count: both still say "21 screens". **The verified number, agreed by three independent lists that are checked against each other automatically, is 29.** |
why: There are at least four stale reference documents, not two, and they are stale at two different wrong values. `grep -rn "21 screens"` finds `packages/vigil-ui/README.md:6,35,89,102` and `knowledge/kb/console-and-ui.md:25` — the two the briefing counted. But `grep -rn "[0-9]* screens"` also finds the repository's front page, `README.md:519` ("bringing the UI to **28 screens**") and `README.md:683` ("One of the UI's **28 screens**"), plus `docs/FEATURES.md:189` ("The NAV model (`app.js`) declares **28 screens**"). FEATURES.md is the repo's exhaustive feature catalogue and README.md is its front page — an assessor grepping for the count will hit those first. The verified 29 is right: `knowledge/system-map/screens.yaml` has 29 `- id:` entries (11 DO / 14 MANAGE / 4 LEARN), `knowledge/system-map/system-map.json` has 29, and the `NAV` array in `packages/vigil-ui/app.js` has 29 — I counted all three.
fix: | **Documentation drift** | Four internal reference documents are stale on the screen count, at two different wrong values: `packages/vigil-ui/README.md` and `knowledge/kb/console-and-ui.md` still say "21 screens"; the top-level `README.md` and `docs/FEATURES.md` still say "28 screens". **The verified number, agreed by three independent lists that are checked against each other automatically, is 29.** |
